title: COURT & CUSTOM HOUSE
spans: C 1800 KING KAMEHAMEHA I CONSTRUCTED BRICK HOUSE AT LAHAINA.
1823- KING KAMEHAMEHA II INVITED NEW ENGLAND MISSIONARIES TO LAHAINA FOR ABOUT A YEAR.
1825 FIRST AMERICAN MISSIONARIES ON MAUI BEGAN WORK HERE.
1828 KING KAMEHAMEHA III LIVED AT LAHAINA MUCH OF THE TIME.
1831 LAHAINALUNA SEMINARY ESTABLISHED FOR TRAINING TEACHERS.
1834 LAHAINALUNA PRESS PRODUCED BOOKS IN HAWAIIAN LANGUAGE.
1830-60 LAHAINA, ANCHORAGE FOR SHIPS OF PACIFIC WHALING FLEET.
1845 MEETING OF FIRST HAWAIIAN CONSTITUTIONAL LEGISLATURE.
1894 ROYAL RESIDENCE AND THE LEGISLATURE MOVED TO HONOLULU.

IN THE 1850'S IT WAS PROPOSED TO ERECT A NEW GOVERNMENT BUILDING TO HOUSE THE COURTS THAT WERE THEN HELD IN THE OLD HALE PULA (KING'S PALACE). GEORGE THOMAS SIGNED A CONTRACT ON JULY 26TH, 1859 TO BUILD A NEW COURT AND CUSTOM HOUSE.

THE TWO-STORY STONE BUILDING WITH A FLAT ROOF AND A VERANDAH. IN FRONT WAS NEARLY COMPLETE IN DECEMBER. AT THAT TIME IT WAS DESCRIBED AS CONTAINING A CUSTOM-HOUSE WITH STORE-ROOM BELOW, A POST OFFICE, A TAX COLLECTOR'S OFFICE WITH VAULT, AN OFFICE FOR THE GOVERNOR, A POLICE COURT, DISTRICT ATTORNEY'S OFFICE, AND A COURTROOM WITH JUDGE'S ROOM AND A JURY ROOM.

REPAIRS WERE MADE IN 1858, IN 1871 (FOLLOWING AN EARTHQUAKE) AND IN 1900. WITH THE INTERIOR WOOD FRAMING IN BAD CONDITION, MAJOR RECONSTRUCTION IN 1925 REPLACED THE FLOOR AND ROOF FRAMING WITH WOOD MEMBERS SUPPORTED ON STEEL BEAMS AND COLUMNS, AND THE CLASSIC PORTICO WAS ADDED. TODAY THE UPPER FLOOR IS OCCUPIED BY THE POLICE DEPARTMENT AND COURT; THE LOWER FLOOR IS PRESENTLY VACATED.

THIS PROJECT WAS FINANCED THROUGH THE COLLABORATION OF THE U.S. NATIONAL PARK SERVICE AND THE LAHAINA RESTORATION FOUNDATION, AND DEVELOPED UNDER THE DIRECTION OF A LEWIS KOUE, SUPERVISING ARCHITECT, HISTORIC AMERICAN BUILDINGS SURVEY, NATIONAL PARK SERVICE.

MEASURED AND DRAWN UNDER THE SUPERVISION OF MELVIN M. ROTSCH, ARCHITECT, TEXAS A&M UNIVERSITY, BY STUDENT ARCHITECTS, E. DAVIS CHAUVIERE OF THE TEXAS A&M UNIVERSITY, RALSTON H. NAGATA OF THE UNIVERSITY OF HAWAII, DON M. SEYFERT OF THE KANSAS STATE UNIVERSITY.
DRAWN BY E. DAVIS CHAUVIERE & DON M. SEYFERT 1966

description: This sheet documents the Court & Custom House in Lahaina, Maui, Hawaii. It features a regional map of the Island of Maui and a detailed site plan of Lahaina town highlighting the building's location near Front Street and Prison Street. Descriptive text outlines the building's history from the 1850s, noting its construction as a two-story stone structure with a flat roof and verandah, serving various governmental functions. The sheet also details later repairs and reconstruction, crediting the Historic American Buildings Survey and student architects from 1966.
